raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> [!TIP]
> **Pairs with ROCm/aiter#6697** (MoE sort folded into GEMM1). With both PRs on the latest main, GLM-5.2 on the InferenceX agentic-trace benchmark gets **+10.6% median interactivity** (290.9 -> 321.7 tok/s/user) and **-9.6% median ITL** vs main. This PR alone: +4.1%. Details under "Speed Tests and Profiling".

## Motivation

With MTP, GLM-5.2 runs the gfx950 DSA indexer logits kernel (`logits_hist`, node 3 of the fused decode indexer) once per verify step on each of its 21 "full" indexer layers. Each request contributes 6 rows (the draft positions), and all 6 rows read the same KV pages, but `logits_hist_m` loads every page once per row. At small batches with long contexts the kernel is bound by those loads.

This PR reads each shared page once per slot of 3 rows, so a request reads each page twice instead of 6 times. The kernel gets up to 2.67x faster, and median interactivity on the InferenceX agentic-trace benchmark (conc 4) rises 4.1%.

## Modifications

- **`paged_mqa_logits.cuh`** adds `logits_hist_slot`. `logits_hist_m` is unchanged; its machine code is identical to main's.
  - The new kernel takes rows in slots of 3. The blocks of a slot split its pages, and every loaded page is scored for each row of the slot, so a page shared by a request's rows is read once per slot. Rows whose page tables differ stream separately.
  - The per-logit math, masking and histogram binning are `logits_hist_m`'s, so logits and histogram are bit-identical.
  - `PagedMqaLogitsKernel::run` takes a new `share_pages` argument and launches the new kernel only when it is set and the grid has at most 18 rows.
- **Where it is used.** The kernel is faster only at long contexts, and it runs inside the decode CUDA graph, so the host decides per graph:
  - On gfx950, `DsaGraphVariants` for the MTP verify graphs captures a third variant, `sparse_shared_pages`.
  - `select()` replays that variant when the batch has at most 18 verify rows and its longest request holds at least 96k tokens.
  - `dsa_indexer` passes `share_pages` (through `gfx950_fused_indexer.py`) only under that variant. Eager calls apply the same rule from `seq_lens_cpu`.
  - Every other launch, including decode without MTP and other GPUs, is main's path.
- **No new flags.**
- **Tests:**
  - `test_logits_hist_shared_pages_matches_per_row`: shared-page vs per-row kernel bitwise on the same rows, for 13 context mixes from 1k to 600k tokens, mixed requests, a graph-width page table, and partial grids down to 1 row.
  - `test_topk_transform_on_shared_page_logits`: node 4 on the new kernel's histogram matches the standard top-k path.
  - `test_dsa_graph_variants.py` (CPU): labels and selection boundaries.
- **Benchmark:** `benchmark/kernels/deepseek/benchmark_dsa_gfx950_logits_hist.py` times both kernels per setup.

## Accuracy Tests

The logits and histogram are bit-identical to `logits_hist_m` in every tested configuration: unit tests, plus every microbenchmark setup, 3 runs each.

End to end, GLM-5.2-MXFP4 on 8x MI355X, with MTP acceptance not simulated. Scored with `sgl-eval run gsm8k` (0.1.3, all 1319 questions, `enable_thinking=false`); main and this PR alternate, 2 runs each:

| round | gsm8k score, main / PR | MTP accept length, main / PR (server counters) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 70.89% / 70.81% | 4.18 / not comparable (one PR-arm request looped greedily to the 1M-token context limit; `max_tokens` was uncapped) |
| 2 (`--max-tokens 4096`) | 70.66% / 70.81% | 4.18 / 4.21 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Kernel.** Each sample is one CUDA graph of 8 launches, each on a different 526 MB KV pool, after a 1 GiB read that evicts L2 and MALL.
- Inputs: 6 rows per request with seqlens ctx-5..ctx; page table 16386 pages wide (GLM-5.2's captured width); fp8 q/KV as in serving.
- Times are medians of 3 fresh processes, in us per launch.
- "main kernel" rows run the same machine code on both sides, so their spread (0.95-1.03 here) is this method's noise.

| verify rows (requests) | longest ctx | kernel this PR runs | main us | PR us | speedup [range] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 (1) | 4k / 24k / 64k | main | 7.34 / 9.49 / 13.61 | same kernel | 1.00 [0.94-1.02] |
| 6 (1) | 96k | shared | 17.23 | 15.57 | 1.11 [1.09-1.11] |
| 6 (1) | 128k | shared | 20.68 | 16.63 | 1.24 [1.23-1.27] |
| 6 (1) | 512k | shared | 61.74 | 27.07 | 2.27 [2.27-2.30] |
| 6 (1) | 1M | shared | 115.03 | 42.70 | 2.67 [2.67-2.69] |
| 12 (2) | 96k | shared | 20.20 | 16.72 | 1.20 [1.20-1.22] |
| 12 (2) | 128k / 512k | shared | 24.42 / 70.96 | 19.01 / 42.55 | 1.28 / 1.67 |
| 12 (2) | 96k + 2k / 256k + 4k | shared | 18.14 / 34.59 | 16.22 / 24.43 | 1.12 / 1.41 |
| 18 (3) | 96k / 128k / 512k | shared | 29.59 / 35.73 / 124.60 | 19.21 / 23.11 / 59.12 | 1.54 / 1.55 / 2.11 |
| 18 (3) | 96k + 4k + 4k / 128k + 32k + 8k | shared | 18.66 / 22.84 | 17.81 / 21.04 | 1.05 / 1.09 |
| <= 18, longest < 96k | | main | | same kernel | 1.00 |
| 24 / 48 | any | main | | same kernel | 1.00 |

Weighting by the (rows, context) mix of a 15-minute InferenceX agentic-trace run at concurrency 4 (987 decode steps, 84% of verify steps at batch 1), the op goes from 33.8 to 20.3 us per call (1.67x).

**End to end.** GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, MTP (EAGLE, 5 steps, 6 draft tokens), the InferenceX CI flags under "How to reproduce", simulated acceptance 3.61 as in that CI. `bench_serving`, random data, fixed lengths, num-prompts = 5 x concurrency; main and this PR alternate on the same node, 2 runs per arm.

| ISL / OSL | conc | median ITL ms, main -> PR | Δ | mean TPOT ms, main -> PR | Δ | output tok/s, main -> PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400k / 1.5k | 1 | 3.09 [3.08-3.09] -> 2.96 [2.95-2.97] | -4.1% | 3.42 [3.41-3.42] -> 3.28 [3.28-3.28] | -3.9% | 58.83 [58.47-59.18] -> 59.44 [59.06-59.82] | +1.0% |
| 400k / 1.5k | 2 | 3.36 [3.34-3.38] -> 3.27 [3.25-3.29] | -2.8% | 11.66 [11.59-11.72] -> 10.71 [9.95-11.48] | -8.1% | 59.32 [59.15-59.49] -> 59.79 [59.63-59.94] | +0.8% |

The kernel's share of a verify step grows with context, so the end-to-end gain shows at long contexts: at 400k, median ITL is -4.1% (conc 1) and -2.8% (conc 2), with non-overlapping ranges.
- At 120k / 2k (conc 1, 2 and 4) the effect is not measurable: median ITL moves by -0.1% to +0.0%, within run-to-run noise, and nothing regresses.
- Output tok/s barely moves at 400k because each request spends about 25 s in prefill, which this PR does not touch.
- Median ITL is the decode-only metric; TPOT at conc 2 also includes the other request's chunked prefill.

**Agentic trace.** This is the InferenceX agentx benchmark that the CI runs for this model:
- TP8, MTP, concurrency 4, 3600 s of the `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126` coding-agent trace through aiperf;
- simulated acceptance 3.61, as in that CI;
- byte-identical prompts in every run.

Main and this PR alternate on one node, 2 runs per arm, each in a fresh container (image v0.5.22-rocm720-20261018 with aiter main 9e2884545 in both arms). In this trace the median request has 63k tokens of context and the p90 has 465k.

| metric | main | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| median interactivity, tok/s/user | 288.3 [284.7-291.9] | 300.1 [300.0-300.1] | +4.1% |
| median ITL, ms | 3.47 [3.43-3.51] | 3.33 [3.33-3.33] | -3.9% |
| p90 interactivity, tok/s/user | 237.5 [234.9-240.1] | 240.7 [236.4-245.1] | +1.4% |
| median TTFT, s | 0.253 [0.251-0.255] | 0.251 [0.248-0.253] | -0.8% |
| output tok/s | 220.4 [216.6-224.1] | 218.1 [216.7-219.5] | -1.0% |

- The interactivity ranges do not overlap: this PR's slower run is still 2.8% above main's faster run.
- Output tok/s follows the generated lengths (temperature 1.0), so it moves within its run-to-run spread.

**Combined with ROCm/aiter#6697.** That PR folds the MoE sort into GEMM1 for the same GLM-5.2 decode path. With both PRs applied to the latest main (sglang 574f9cdb, aiter 45d7ef38), the same agentic-trace benchmark gives +10.6% median interactivity (290.9 -> 321.7) and -9.6% median ITL against main. That is one 1800 s run per arm. The two gains compound: 1.041 x 1.064 = 1.108.

**Startup cost.** The third verify-graph variant is captured for every bs, though only bs 1-3 use the new kernel. It adds 2.8 s to the target-verify graph capture (25.3 s -> 28.1 s for bs 1-8) and 0.02 GB of graph memory (1.10 -> 1.12 GB).

**Profile.** Capture traces (`--enable-profile-cuda-graph`, `SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE=1`) record the kernel of every launch in every captured verify graph.
- With this PR, the `sparse_shared_pages` graphs for bs 1-3 launch `logits_hist_slot` 21 times (once per full indexer layer) and `logits_hist_m` zero times, on all 8 ranks.
- Every other graph launches `logits_hist_m` 21 times: the dense and sparse graphs at every bs, and the shared-page graphs at bs 4-8, which keep the per-row kernel.
- On main, every graph launches `logits_hist_m`.
- In eager mode, a 120k-token request runs only `logits_hist_slot` on all 8 ranks.

## How to reproduce

Hardware: 8x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.0. Image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.22-rocm720-mi35x-20261018`, whose sglang e9b22a08 matches main for every file this PR touches; for the PR arm, this branch's files are copied over. Model: amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4.

```bash
python3 test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dsa_graph_variants.py
python3 test/registered/amd/test_dsa_gfx950_fused_indexer.py -v          # one gfx950 GPU
python3 benchmark/kernels/deepseek/benchmark_dsa_gfx950_logits_hist.py --ctx 4096 131072 524288
# server (InferenceX CI 37326853365 flags); the SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_* variables are dropped for accuracy runs
SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=true SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected \
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --dsa-prefill-backend triton --dsa-decode-backend triton \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-input-len 400000 \
  --random-output-len 1500 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompts 5
sgl-eval run gsm8k --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --num-threads 8 --chat-template-kwarg enable_thinking=false
```

## Known gaps

- The 96k cut-over and the blocks-per-row choices were measured on MI355X for 6-draft-token verify grids. With another draft count the rows-to-batch mapping changes, but the rule is expressed in rows, so it still applies; it was not separately tuned.
- Batches of 1-3 requests whose longest context is under 96k keep main's kernel. The new kernel is slower there, mainly because its larger LDS footprint gives fewer blocks per row.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).


## Known gaps

- The 96k cut-over and the blocks-per-row choices were measured on MI355X for 6-draft-token verify grids. With another draft count the rows-to-batch mapping changes, but the rule is expressed in rows, so it still applies; it was not separately tuned.
- Batches of 1-3 requests whose longest context is under 96k keep main's kernel. The new kernel is slower there, mainly because its larger LDS footprint gives fewer blocks per row.

@@ -0,0 +1,137 @@
+"""Latency of the gfx950 DSA indexer logits kernel (node 3 of the fused decode
+indexer) on MTP verify grids: 6 rows per request sharing one page table.
+
+Each sample is one CUDA graph replay of NUM_LAYERS launches, each reading a
+different KV pool (as the layers of a decode step do), after a 1 GiB read that
+evicts L2 and MALL; the reported time is graph time / NUM_LAYERS.  Each setup is
+timed with the per-row kernel and with the shared-page kernel (share_pages);
+the server selects the shared-page kernel only for <= 18 rows whose longest
+context is >= 96k tokens.
+
+    python benchmark/kernels/deepseek/benchmark_dsa_gfx950_logits_hist.py
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import math
+import statistics
+
+import torch
+
+FP8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn
+PAGE_SIZE = 64
+PAGE_BYTES = PAGE_SIZE * 132
+K_BYTES = PAGE_SIZE * 128
+POOL_PAGES = 62280  # ~526 MB per layer, larger than MALL
+TABLE_PAGES = 16386  # GLM-5.2's captured page-table width
+
+
+def make_pool(gen):
+    u8 = torch.empty(POOL_PAGES, PAGE_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    for s in range(0, POOL_PAGES, 8192):
+        e = min(POOL_PAGES, s + 8192)
+        n = e - s
+        u8[s:e, :K_BYTES] = (
+            (0.7 * torch.randn(n, K_BYTES, generator=gen, device="cuda"))
+            .to(FP8)
+            .view(torch.uint8)
+        )
+        scale = torch.exp2(
+            -8 + 2 * torch.rand(n, PAGE_SIZE, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+        )
+        u8[s:e, K_BYTES:] = scale.view(torch.uint8)
+    return u8.view(FP8)
+
+
+def bench(mod, bpr, share, ctxs, pools, gen, flush, iters):
+    rows = 6 * len(ctxs)
+    perm = torch.randperm(POOL_PAGES, generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(1))
+    table = torch.zeros(rows, TABLE_PAGES, dtype=torch.int32)
+    seqlens, off = [], 0
+    for i, c in enumerate(ctxs):
+        n = math.ceil(c / PAGE_SIZE)
+        table[6 * i : 6 * i + 6, :n] = perm[
+            torch.arange(off, off + n) % POOL_PAGES
+        ].int()
+        off += n
+        seqlens += [c - 5 + j for j in range(6)]
+    table = table.cuda()
+    seqlens = torch.tensor(seqlens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    q = (2.0 * torch.randn(rows, 32, 128, generator=gen, device="cuda")).to(FP8)
+    gate = torch.rand(rows, 32, generator=gen, device="cuda") * 0.02
+    out = torch.empty(rows, TABLE_PAGES * PAGE_SIZE, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    ghist = torch.zeros(rows, 4096 + 64, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    def run():
+        for kv in pools:
+            mod.logits_hist(q, kv, gate, seqlens, table, out, ghist, bpr, share)
+
+    s = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(s):
+        run()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        run()
+    sink = torch.empty((), device="cuda")
+    times = []
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        torch.sum(flush, dim=0, out=sink)
+        a, b = (
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+            torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True),
+        )
+        a.record()
+        graph.replay()
+        b.record()
+        b.synchronize()
+        times.append(a.elapsed_time(b) * 1e3 / len(pools))
+    return statistics.median(times)
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--requests", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 2, 3])
+    ap.add_argument(
+        "--ctx",
+        type=int,
+        nargs="+",
+        default=[4096, 32768, 65536, 131072, 262144, 524288],
+    )
+    ap.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=8)
+    ap.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=200)
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsa.hip_gfx950 import loader
+
+    mod = loader.modules()[2]
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+    pools = [make_pool(gen) for _ in range(a.layers)]
+    flush = torch.ones((1 << 30) // 4, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    print(
+        f"{'requests':>8} {'rows':>4} {'ctx':>8} {'per-row us':>10} "
+        f"{'shared us':>10} {'speedup':>8}"
+    )
+    for reqs in a.requests:
+        for c in a.ctx:
+            us = [
+                bench(
+                    mod,
+                    loader.LOGITS_BLOCKS_PER_ROW,
+                    share,
+                    [c] * reqs,
+                    pools,
+                    gen,
+                    flush,
+                    a.iters,
+                )
+                for share in (0, 1)
+            ]
+            print(
+                f"{reqs:>8} {6 * reqs:>4} {c:>8} {us[0]:>10.2f} {us[1]:>10.2f} "
+                f"{us[0] / us[1]:>7.2f}x"
+            )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Tests for the DSA decode/verify CUDA-graph variant selection."""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.graph_variants import (
+    DSA_DENSE,
+    DSA_SPARSE,
+    DSA_SPARSE_SHARED_PAGES,
+    DsaGraphVariants,
+    dsa_max_kv_len,
+    dsa_share_logits_pages,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+def _batch(seq_lens):
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        seq_lens_cpu=torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int64),
+        seq_lens=None,
+        batch_size=len(seq_lens),
+    )
+
+
+class TestDsaGraphVariants(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_labels(self):
+        self.assertEqual(DsaGraphVariants(2048).capture_labels, (DSA_DENSE, DSA_SPARSE))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            DsaGraphVariants(2048, verify_rows_per_req=6).capture_labels,
+            (DSA_DENSE, DSA_SPARSE, DSA_SPARSE_SHARED_PAGES),
+        )
+
+    def test_without_verify_rows_never_shares_pages(self):
+        v = DsaGraphVariants(2048)
+        self.assertEqual(v.select(_batch([1000])), DSA_DENSE)
+        self.assertEqual(v.select(_batch([500000])), DSA_SPARSE)
+
+    def test_verify_selection(self):
+        v = DsaGraphVariants(2048, verify_rows_per_req=6)
+        cases = [
+            ([2048], DSA_DENSE),
+            ([2049], DSA_SPARSE),
+            ([98303], DSA_SPARSE),
+            ([98304], DSA_SPARSE_SHARED_PAGES),
+            ([5000, 98304], DSA_SPARSE_SHARED_PAGES),
+            ([98303, 100, 100], DSA_SPARSE),
+            ([98304, 100, 100], DSA_SPARSE_SHARED_PAGES),
+            ([500000] * 4, DSA_SPARSE),  # 24 rows keep the per-row kernel
+        ]
+        for lens, want in cases:
+            with self.subTest(lens=lens):
+                self.assertEqual(v.select(_batch(lens)), want)
+
+    def test_lengths_fall_back_to_device_tensor(self):
+        """Verify batches can carry an empty host mirror; the device lengths decide."""
+        v = DsaGraphVariants(2048, verify_rows_per_req=6)
+        batch = SimpleNamespace(
+            seq_lens_cpu=torch.empty((0,), dtype=torch.int64),
+            seq_lens=torch.tensor([120000]),
+            batch_size=1,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(v.select(batch), DSA_SPARSE_SHARED_PAGES)
+        self.assertEqual(dsa_max_kv_len(batch), 120000)
+
+    def test_share_logits_pages(self):
+        self.assertTrue(dsa_share_logits_pages(6, 98304))
+        self.assertFalse(dsa_share_logits_pages(6, 98303))
+        self.assertTrue(dsa_share_logits_pages(18, 98304))
+        self.assertFalse(dsa_share_logits_pages(19, 10**6))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
